easy.question: Who bought Joseph in Egypt?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Potiphar bought Joseph from the Ishmaelites.

easy.question: In which land was Joseph after he was brought there?
easy.explanation: Joseph was brought down to Egypt.

easy.question: What did Potiphar put Joseph in charge of?
answers: His house and all his property
easy.explanation: Potiphar put Joseph in charge of his house and everything he owned.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: Joseph was put in charge of the house, then bought, and finally prospered
Joseph was bought, prospered, and then put in charge of Potiphar’s house
Joseph prospered, was sold to Potiphar, and then went down to Egypt
medium.explanation: Joseph was first bought in Egypt, then the Lord prospered him, and finally Potiphar put him in charge of his house.

medium.question: What does the phrase “Joseph found grace in his sight” mean?
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Potiphar viewed Joseph favorably and gave him an important position.

medium.question: According to the verse, what did Potiphar personally keep track of?
medium.explanation: Potiphar left everything in Joseph’s hands and knew nothing about it except the bread he ate.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that Potiphar knew nothing about anything he owned?
answers: He trusted Joseph greatly to manage his property
Joseph did not work in his house
challenge.explanation: Potiphar’s lack of involvement with his property shows that he greatly trusted Joseph.

challenge.question: How extensive was the blessing that came to the Egyptian’s household because of Joseph?
answers: Both the house and the field were blessed
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the Lord’s blessing was on everything Potiphar had, both in the house and in the field.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that Potiphar understood Joseph’s success to be connected with the Lord?
answers: Potiphar saw that Joseph was handsome
Potiphar gave Joseph only the bread
Potiphar saw that the Lord was with Joseph and prospered all he did
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that Potiphar saw the Lord was with Joseph and made everything he did prosper.

easy.question: Who said to Joseph, “Lie with me”?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Joseph’s master’s wife asked him to lie with her.

easy.question: How did Joseph respond to his master’s wife?
answers: He ran away from the house
easy.explanation: The verse says that Joseph refused.

easy.question: Whom did Joseph say he would sin against if he did this wicked thing?
easy.explanation: Joseph said, “How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?”

medium.question: Why did Joseph regard his master’s wife’s request as a serious matter?
answers: It would betray his master’s trust and be a sin against God
He did not want to work in the house
She was a foreigner in the land
medium.explanation: Joseph said that his master had entrusted everything to him, and that the act would be a sin against God.

medium.question: According to the verse, what had Joseph’s master not kept back from him?
medium.explanation: Joseph said that his master had withheld nothing from him except his wife.

medium.question: What did his master’s wife do after Joseph refused her?
answers: She asked her husband to dismiss Joseph
She continued speaking to Joseph day after day
medium.explanation: The verse says that she spoke to Joseph day by day, but he would not listen to her.

challenge.question: Which central reason shows that Joseph regarded the act as especially serious?
answers: It would betray his master’s trust and be a sin against God
It was forbidden only because Joseph was a servant
It might cause Joseph to lose his job
challenge.explanation: Joseph emphasized both his master’s trust and the sin against God, calling it “this great wickedness.”

challenge.question: What does “he hearkened not unto her” mean in this context?

Joseph did not respond to or agree with her
Joseph asked her to speak more loudly
challenge.explanation: Since she spoke to him repeatedly, the phrase means that Joseph would not listen to or obey her.

answers: All the property in the house
His wife, because she was his master’s wife
challenge.explanation: Joseph said that his master had entrusted everything to him except his wife.

paragraphs.title: Joseph Flees, Leaving His Garment Behind

easy.question: Why did Joseph go into the house?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Joseph went into the house to do his business.

easy.question: Who was not in the house at that time?
answers: Any of the men of the household
easy.explanation: The verse says that none of the men of the house was there.

easy.question: What did Joseph do after Potiphar’s wife caught him by his garment?
answers: He left the garment in her hand and fled outside
easy.explanation: Joseph left his garment in her hand, fled, and got out.

medium.question: Why was Joseph alone in the house at that time?
answers: None of the household men were there
Potiphar’s wife had left the house
medium.explanation: The verse specifically says that none of the men of the house was there.

medium.question: What was Joseph doing when he went into the house?
medium.explanation: The verse says that Joseph went into the house to do his business, meaning his work.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: Joseph fled, then came to work, and then was caught by his garment
Joseph came to do his work, was caught by his garment, and then fled
Joseph was caught by his garment, fled, and then entered the house
medium.explanation: Joseph first entered the house to work, then the woman caught his garment, and finally he fled outside.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Joseph leaving his garment and fleeing?
answers: He chose to get away immediately, even at the cost of losing the garment
He wanted to remain with the woman
He forgot why he had entered the house
challenge.explanation: Leaving the garment shows that Joseph chose immediate escape, even though the garment remained in her hand.

challenge.question: What striking contrast is described in these verses?
answers: Joseph entered the house to work, but left it by fleeing
Joseph entered the house to sleep, but left it to work
Joseph entered with the household men, but left with them
challenge.explanation: Joseph entered for the ordinary purpose of working, but fled after the woman seized his garment.

challenge.question: What exact detail does the verse emphasize about Joseph’s garment?
answers: It remained in the woman’s hand
Joseph gave it to the household men
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that Joseph left his garment in her hand instead of taking it with him.

answers: He chose to get away immediately, even at the cost of losing the garment

Joseph gave it to the household men
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that Joseph left his garment in her hand instead of taking it with him.

easy.question: What did Joseph do when his garment remained in her hand?
easy.explanation: When the garment remained in her hand, Joseph fled and got out.

easy.question: Whom did Potiphar’s wife call after Joseph left?
easy.explanation: The verse says that she called the men of her household.

easy.question: What remained in Potiphar’s wife’s possession?
easy.explanation: The garment that Joseph left behind remained with her.

medium.question: Why did Potiphar’s wife say that she cried out with a loud voice?
answers: She claimed that Joseph came in to lie with her
She wanted to call Joseph back
medium.explanation: She claimed that Joseph came to her to lie with her, so she cried out loudly.

medium.question: What did Potiphar’s wife do with the garment until her husband came home?
answers: She gave it to the household men
medium.explanation: The verse says that she laid the garment beside her until her husband came home.

medium.question: What does “to mock us” mean in the context of her accusation?
answers: To behave sexually or make advances
medium.explanation: In this accusation, the phrase refers to improper sexual behavior or advances.

challenge.question: Which detail in Potiphar’s wife’s words shows that she also tried to blame her husband?
answers: She said, “He hath brought in an Hebrew unto us”
She said that Joseph went outside
She kept the garment beside her
challenge.explanation: By saying “he hath brought in,” she reminded Potiphar that he himself had brought Joseph into the house.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that Potiphar’s wife told the same story to the household men and then to her husband?
answers: She wanted to establish a consistent story against Joseph
challenge.explanation: Repeating the same account to different people helped her strengthen her accusation against Joseph.

challenge.question: What practical reason might explain why Joseph did not take his garment when he fled?
answers: He wanted to leave her a gift
He did not notice that it had fallen
He preferred to escape immediately, even if the garment was left behind
challenge.explanation: The repeated description of Joseph fleeing and leaving the garment emphasizes his immediate escape from danger.

easy.question: Who heard what Potiphar’s wife said about Joseph?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Joseph’s master heard his wife’s words.

easy.question: What did Joseph’s master do to him?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Joseph’s master put him in prison.

easy.question: Where was Joseph afterward?
easy.explanation: The verse ends by saying that Joseph was in prison.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in these verses?
answers: The master heard, became angry, and put Joseph in prison
Joseph fled, and then the master heard his wife
The master released Joseph, and then became angry
medium.explanation: First the master heard his wife’s words, then his anger was kindled, and finally he put Joseph in prison.

medium.question: What happened when Joseph’s master heard his wife’s words?
medium.explanation: The phrase “his wrath was kindled” means that he became angry.

medium.question: Why does the verse identify the prison as the place where the king’s prisoners were bound?
answers: To say that Joseph was a king
To explain that Joseph was not in Egypt
To identify it as a prison for the king’s prisoners
medium.explanation: The verse describes the prison as the place where the king’s prisoners were held.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that Joseph’s master put him in prison rather than killing him?
challenge.explanation: Although the master was angry, the punishment described was putting Joseph in prison.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “the king’s prisoners” indicate about the people held in the prison?
answers: They were connected with the king or his government
They were only soldiers from Canaan
challenge.explanation: The phrase identifies them as prisoners connected with the king and his authority.

challenge.question: What special significance may be understood from describing the prison as a place for the king’s prisoners?
answers: It was an open place without guards
It was a prison connected with royal authority
challenge.explanation: The reference to the king’s prisoners suggests that the prison was connected with the royal administration.

easy.question: Who was with Joseph?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord was with Joseph.”

easy.question: Who put the prisoners and everything done in the prison into Joseph’s hands?
easy.explanation: The keeper of the prison entrusted all the prisoners and the work to Joseph.

easy.question: What did Joseph do in the prison?
answers: He managed everything that was done there
easy.explanation: The verse says that Joseph was responsible for everything done in the prison.

medium.question: Why did the keeper of the prison entrust all the prison’s affairs to Joseph?
answers: The Lord was with Joseph and prospered what he did
medium.explanation: The verses connect the Lord’s presence with Joseph and his success to the keeper’s trust in him.

medium.question: What does the phrase “gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison” mean?
answers: The keeper of the prison viewed Joseph positively
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the keeper regarded Joseph favorably.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in these verses?
answers: Joseph was released, and then entered the prison
The keeper punished Joseph, and then the Lord left him
The Lord was with Joseph, the keeper gave him responsibility, and Joseph prospered
medium.explanation: The verses first describe the Lord’s help, then Joseph’s responsibility, and finally his success.

answers: He trusted Joseph and did not inspect everything he did
Joseph did no work at all
challenge.explanation: The statement shows that the keeper trusted Joseph completely and did not need to supervise every detail.

challenge.question: What idea is shared by verses 21 and 23?
answers: The Lord was with Joseph and brought him success
The keeper of the prison became a prisoner
challenge.explanation: Both verses emphasize that the Lord was with Joseph, and verse 23 says that the Lord prospered his work.

challenge.question: According to the verse, who was the ultimate source of Joseph’s success, even though Joseph did the work himself?
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the Lord made whatever Joseph did prosper.
